page: Microsoft Azure D16as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V74 processors. The instance provides 16 vCPUs backed by 8 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading at clock speeds up to 3.7 GHz. System memory totals 64 GB, offering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions such as VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute capabilities, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests ranking in the top quartile of evaluated systems. Multi-threaded evaluations, including Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics, land squarely in the mid-range expected for a 16-thread profile. While cached memory bandwidth performs competitively, uncached large-block read operations register lower throughput, reflecting a trade-off in memory-bus traversal for very large datasets.

The D16as_v6 includes zero bundled local storage, operating as a diskless compute node that relies entirely on remote Azure Premium Storage attachments for persistent data needs. Additionally, it does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which maintains a clean compute-to-cost profile focused purely on standard enterprise compute execution.

This hardware balance makes the instance well-suited for general-purpose applications such as web application clusters, microservice orchestration, Redis caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines. It handles single-threaded latency-sensitive code and moderate container density effectively, while workloads demanding ultra-low-latency local disk I/O or massive parallel GPU execution should look to storage-optimized or accelerated families.

Compute performance is characterized by strong single-core benchmarks and solid multi-core execution, supported by hardware AVX-512 extensions. The server does not include bundled local disk storage or GPU acceleration, relying on remote managed disks for persistence. Given this architectural profile, the D16as_v6 offers balanced resource density suited for mid-sized relational database frontends, API servers, Redis nodes, and continuous integration environments requiring dependable CPU cycles without dedicated storage hardware overhead.
